verdict.rationale: ReadMe offers 'Bi-directional sync' that creates a two-way connection between a ReadMe project and a GitHub/GitLab repo, letting you write in your local git setup, and a GitHub AI Writer that watches pull requests to propose doc updates when code changes — evidence of a git-integrated workflow. The official rdme CLI (confirmed runnable via npx) further enables CI/CD-driven doc publishing. However, ReadMe's own docs frame the ReadMe hub/database as the primary source of truth with sync back and forth, rather than git branches/PRs/merges being the authoritative trigger for what gets published — there's no documented branch-preview-per-PR or merge-triggers-deploy pipeline akin to true docs-as-code tools. Missing for 10: explicit branch-per-PR preview builds, merge-to-publish CI pipeline documentation, and independent confirmation that git remains the sole source of truth rather than ReadMe's own versioning system.
